speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Mr Leon Perera also expressed the desire that we must be aware of minorities who seek to sow discord amongst numerical majorities through influence and interference, sow discord along the lines of what the terrorism regime seeks.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And I agree that that is a good desire to have.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But I would also say that the laws in Singapore already deter such behaviour.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The Government has already put in the legal levers to deal with this.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I had mentioned the Public Order Act, Sedition Act and the Penal Code in the opening speech.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: All these seek, in one way or another, to deter the proliferation of violent extremism, radical teachings.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: He suggested the use of religious knowledge in schools to achieve that.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But I think Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap would agree that much would depend on the curriculum and teaching materials of the subject, and that one requirement would be that the subject not include teachings that would incite violent extremism.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: That should be avoided so as not to manipulate the students.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Many of the Members here shared how multiracialism was furthered in their communities.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: As Ms Thanaletchimi stated, as our Singapore workforce constituents comprise a combination of local and migrant workers, it is not only important to inculcate the value of multiracialism and multiculturalism among Singaporeans but also to the migrant workers from various countries.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And in preserving it, Mr Pritam Singh shared with us that conflicts of another country, although emotive, should not be transported here to destroy the social fabric we have in Singapore − our common humanity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: When I was crafting the Motion, it was to view terrorism as an enemy in a real sense.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: After all, terrorism is an affront to Singapore and all her values.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I thought "weapon" was a good analogy for what we are up against, and the hybrid word "socio-weapon" was chosen because terrorism is a common enemy we have to battle against as a citizenry.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In peacetime, we do not use multiracialism as a weapon.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But when under attack, we can deploy that multiracialism as a strength, as a weapon, against the common enemy.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It is distinct from the hardware the SAF and Home Team will use, but it is as important a tool, as important a weapon when we are facing a terrorist attack on our shores.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Hence, the reason for the word "socio-weapon" in the Motion's title.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I am sure many other constituencies have conducted similar exercises.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Different people from different races are playing a part now to prepare for the consequences of a terror attack.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: As Minister K Shanmugam stated clearly, we have never believed that a laissez-faire approach to creating a national identity would work.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We are wanting to secure a multiracial society that will work and that we are activist in this respect.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: As Minister Yaacob Ibrahim said passionately, we all sing the same National Anthem and hold our right fist to our hearts when reciting the pledge.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: These and many more experiences of being a Singaporean must mean something to every one of us, especially when the going gets tough for a member of our Singaporean family.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Dr Mercy Jesuvadian of the National Institute of Education highlighted that it is important to start building racial harmony at an early age.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: At the PAP Community Foundation (PCF) Sparkle Tots Preschool in my constituency, we have babies of all the different races taken care of by infant care teachers of different races.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Members can see multiracial babies and multiracial infant caregivers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: There is multiracial bonding on all levels − the teacher with the infant, the infants with one another, the teacher with her colleagues, the infant's family and the teacher, and the families with other families.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But this also shows the big reservoir of trust we have among the races − to augment Dr Tan Wu Meng's point − to be able to entrust the baby with someone else from a different race.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It is reflective of these day-after banners, which Ulu Pandan residents helped to organise, reflective of the values Singapore aspires to achieve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Many of us here celebrate Multiracial Day in our constituencies where the children dress up in traditional costumes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Recently, in Ulu Pandan, we had a Multiracial Dessert Day.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We feasted on many different kinds of desserts, from ang ku kueh, roti, samosa, pineapple tarts.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We experienced the wonder of multiracialism through our appetites and stomachs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: In a very real way, we tasted how each culture had something unique to offer, how each culture was unique and valuable.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And we experienced it in one of the most Singaporean ways possible − food − a language that transcends the different communities.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Many of us would have attended moon cake festivals over the weekend and seen residents of many races carry lanterns together, lighting up the evening with the warm glow of the lanterns.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I took this photograph when visiting the PCF infant care centre in my ward earlier this year.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It is a photograph of Makcik Minaseh carrying young Xander, holding him, caring for him.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It reminded me of what happened 40 years ago.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Back then, I was just born and my parents lived on Changi Air Base.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My father and mother had asked a young Malay lady, Cik Zainap, whether she would like to help my mother in taking care of the children.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My father was flying fighters then in the 1970s.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Pilots' wives went through quite a lot then, not knowing if something would happen in the air to their husbands.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, any extra help at home was very welcomed by my mother.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: She worked well with my mother and she saw my sister and I grow up.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Even after we settled down and started our own families, our family kept in touch with Zainap.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: She is now known as Nenek Zainap to our children and she considers them each her cucu.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: This photograph was taken when my parents, my wife and I and our children visited Zainap last year in her Tampines home for Hari Raya.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Since then, we had our No 3 − so one more cucu for her!

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, it is wonderful that in Singapore, we can consider one another as part of the same keluarga, the same family.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My parents and I are a part of her family, and she is a part of ours.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Mr Choo believed in a Singaporean Singapore, with multiracialism as a bedrock.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Every year since then, we have given out a scholarship to a new and deserving student.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: She is pictured here with Mr Choo's widow, Mr Choo's son Roland, and Mr Choo's grandchildren.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But his values of a united multiracial society within an independent Singapore live on in Waseemah, who is part of the Youth Executive Committee in Ulu Pandan serving a multiracial Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: When terror strikes, what instincts will come to my mind?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The care of Nenek Zainap, the complete dedication of Mr Choo, the effort of Waseemah and the selfless work of the many volunteers and Singaporeans who aspire to multiracialism.
